column6: The original paragraph describes suffering as the endurance of pain, implying a passive experience, while the back-translated paragraph describes it as resistance to pain, suggesting an active struggle against it. This change alters the conceptual understanding of suffering from a state of enduring to one of opposing.
column7: Suffering is the endurance of pain-physical, emotional, mental, or spiritual-especially when prolonged or intense.
column8: Suffering is the resistance to pain-physical, emotional, mental, or spiritual-especially when prolonged or intense.
